# YASAG - Yet Another Space Alien Game

*README.MD file mostly generated by Anthropic's Claude AI because Thomas Dzubin hates documenting code.  LOL*

**YASAG V2.00A** is the **hardware-independent** edition of
[picocalc-space-game](https://github.com/Dzubin/picocalc-space-game) - steer a ship, fire torpedoes at
square aliens, don't get rammed. The V1.xx line is picocalc-space-game and runs
on the ClockworkPi PicoCalc only; V2.xx is the *same gameplay* with every
hardware operation behind a HAL, so **one C codebase** builds for several
machines:

| Target | Hardware | Backend |
|---|---|---|
| `picocalc`  | ClockworkPi PicoCalc (RP2040 / RP2350) | Raspberry Pi Pico SDK + vendored `picocalc-text-starter` drivers |
| `picosystem`| Pimoroni PicoSystem (RP2040)           | bare Pico SDK (ST7789 240x240, PWM piezo, buttons) - *Stage 4* |
| `sdl`       | Windows / Linux                        | SDL2 (static on Windows, shared `libSDL2` shipped beside the executable on Linux) |

The game logic is picocalc-space-game **V1.00A**, unchanged (the 320x320
PicoCalc build is byte-for-byte identical). `picocalc-space-game` itself is
frozen; the small UX changes made here can be backported there separately.

## Status

**Stage 1 (isolation) complete.** All PicoCalc/Pico-SDK/`picocalc-text-starter`
calls are behind the HAL in [`hal/hal.h`](hal/hal.h); [`game/game.c`](game/game.c)
contains no `pico/`, `hardware/`, `drivers/`, or `SDL` include.

**Stage 2a (resolution-independent layout) complete.** Every geometry `#define`
in [`game/game.h`](game/game.h) is now `SCALE_X/Y/S(...)` of its 320x320 base
value (see `hal/hal.h`). At 320x320 with `YASAG_TEXT_SCALE 1` all of them are
the identity - **the PicoCalc build is byte-for-byte V1.00A (compiler-verified:
every int + float macro matches)**. On a 4:3 screen the play box gets
proportionally wider (bigger starfield); sprites and world speeds scale
uniformly so squares stay square; text scales by the integer `YASAG_TEXT_SCALE`.

**Stage 2 (SDL2 backend) complete.** [`hal/hal_sdl.c`](hal/hal_sdl.c) +
[`hal/screenshot_sdl.c`](hal/screenshot_sdl.c) + the `sdl` CMake branch.
`-DYASAG_TARGET=sdl` builds a **fully standalone** `yasag-Windows.exe` (static SDL2 +
static libgcc/libstdc++/winpthread - no non-system DLLs) that runs the game in
a native **640x480** window. Software only: the RGB565 stand-in buffer is
dirty-rect `SDL_BlitSurface`/`SDL_BlitScaled`'d to the window surface each
`vid_present()` (called from `hal_sleep_ms()`, once per frame); no
`SDL_Renderer`. Audio is a square-wave callback; `hal_sleep_ms()` also pumps the
event queue so the win jingle can't freeze the window. `YASAG_SDL_ZOOM` (default
1 = native; 0 = auto-fit desktop; N = force NxN). `YASAG_SDL_SCRIPT` (env, inert
otherwise) feeds timed synthetic keys for head-less screenshots / regression runs.

**Stage 3 (menu / screen polish) complete** - verified running on Windows 11.
- `text.c` gains `text_set_scale()` - runtime glyph magnification. The dense
  **controls / help** legend and the `?`-pause drop to 1x (small crisp cells,
  fits any screen); the status line and menus stay at `YASAG_TEXT_SCALE`. No-op on the
  MCUs (scale is always 1), so **PicoCalc output is unchanged**.
- `big_text()` now scales by `scale * YASAG_TEXT_SCALE`, so the title cards /
  `YOU WON IN` / hints are as big relative to the screen on desktop as on the
  LCD. New `big_text_centered()` centres on `SCREEN_W`.
- **Splash: Up/Down move a `>` cursor over the four difficulty rows, Enter (or
  Space) picks it; 0-3 still jump straight in.** On the PicoCalc the only change
  from V1.00A is that `>` marker and the reworded prompt line (this UX change
  applies to every target; back-port to `picocalc-space-game` is optional).
- The SDL coordinate readout is dropped when its row would fall off the panel
  (least-critical readout; always on at 320x320).

`picocalc` and `sdl` build today; `picosystem` is Stage 4.

## Layout

```
game/       portable core - no hardware headers, same on every target
  game.c/.h   the game (picocalc-space-game V1.00A, HAL calls swapped in)
  text.c/.h   fixed 8x10-cell text on vid_fill_rect() (replaces lcd_putstr)
  font_8x10.c vendored glyph data - MIT, (c) Blair Leduc (picocalc-text-starter)
  font.h      glyph-table interface (no pico dependency)
  screenshot.h  screenshot_capture() - implemented per target
hal/
  hal.h              the seam: vid_ / inp_ / snd_ / hal_time_ + SCALE_* + KEY_*
  hal_picocalc.c     forwards to the vendored starter drivers
  hal_sdl.c/.h       SDL2: RGB565 stand-in buffer -> window surface; sq-wave audio
  screenshot_picocalc.c   ST7789 GRAM read-back -> 24-bit BMP on SD
  screenshot_sdl.c        stand-in buffer      -> 24-bit BMP beside the exe
third_party/
  picocalc-text-starter-main/   vendored, read-only: Blair's code of 2026-10-18 plus four small fixes in drivers/fat32.c, sdcard.c and lcd.c (picocalc target only)
```

The HAL contract (rendering model, input event shape, audio, timing) is
documented in [`hal/hal.h`](hal/hal.h). Key decision: **no framebuffer in the
game** - it draws incrementally through `vid_fill_rect()` on every target; the
SDL backend keeps one private RGB565 stand-in buffer for the absent panel.

## Building

Build + compile happens on a separate machine. Plain **make** (not Ninja):

**PicoCalc** (needs `PICO_SDK_PATH`, or the VS Code Pico extension):

```
cmake -B build -G "Unix Makefiles" -DYASAG_TARGET=picocalc -DPICO_BOARD=pico
make -C build
```

Use `-DPICO_BOARD=pico2` for RP2350. Output: `build/yasag-<chip>.uf2` (`<chip>` is `RP2350` or `RP2040`, matching the board), which the build
also copies to the top-level folder as `yasag-RP2040.uf2` or `yasag-RP2350.uf2`
(by board), so both chips' builds sit side by side - flash by
holding BOOTSEL on power-up, or pressing `~` (Shift+backtick) in the game, then
copying it onto the `RPI-RP2` drive.

**SDL (Windows / Linux)** - needs SDL2 findable by `find_package(SDL2)` (static
lib preferred). With MSYS2: `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-{gcc,cmake,SDL2}`.

```
cmake -B build -G "Unix Makefiles" -DYASAG_TARGET=sdl
make -C build
./yasag-Linux        # or yasag-Windows.exe on Windows
```

The finished executable is named for its platform (`yasag-Windows.exe` /
`yasag-Linux`) and is copied from `build/` to the top-level folder.

Renders at **640x480** in a native-size window.  `-DYASAG_SDL_ZOOM=2` (or `3`)
for a bigger blocky window, `=0` to auto-pick the largest that fits the desktop.
`-DYASAG_SCREEN_W=... -DYASAG_SCREEN_H=...` overrides the render size (on any
target).

The **Windows** build links SDL2 statically -> a single `yasag-Windows.exe`, no DLLs.
The **Linux** build links the shared `libSDL2` (needs the SDL2 development package,
e.g. `libsdl2-dev`, to build) and the build copies that library next to the
executable as `libSDL2-2.0.so.0`, into `build/` and the top-level folder; the
executable finds it through an `$ORIGIN` run-path, so ship `yasag-Linux` and
`libSDL2-2.0.so.0` together.

## Running the SDL build (players)

**Windows**

1. Put `yasag-Windows.exe` anywhere and run it (double-click, or
   `yasag-Windows.exe` in a terminal). Nothing to install - SDL2 is baked in.
2. First run, Windows may warn *"Windows protected your PC"* (the binary is
   unsigned): **More info -> Run anyway**.

**Linux**

1. Keep `yasag-Linux` and `libSDL2-2.0.so.0` in the same folder - the game finds
   that bundled SDL2 automatically and there is nothing to install. (Only if you
   would rather not use the bundled copy, delete it and install the SDL2 runtime
   from your distribution instead:)

   | Distro | Command |
   |---|---|
   | Debian / Ubuntu / Mint | `sudo apt install libsdl2-2.0-0` |
   | Fedora | `sudo dnf install SDL2` |
   | Arch / Manjaro | `sudo pacman -S sdl2` |
   | openSUSE | `sudo zypper install libSDL2-2_0-0` |

2. `chmod +x yasag-Linux` (if it isn't already), then `./yasag-Linux`.

Controls: arrow keys steer, **Space** fires, **S** shields, **C** cloak,
**Enter** flip-and-burn, **A**/**M** autopilot, **?** help, **Q** quit,
Esc or closing the window exits.
